solvedExamples.q: Which of the following pairs of book and author is **NOT** correctly matched?
options: India Wins Freedom — Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
The Discovery of India — Jawaharlal Nehru
solvedExamples.solution: *Hind Swaraj* (1909) was written by **M.K. Gandhi** on board a ship from London to South Africa. Tilak's famous works are *Gita Rahasya* and *The Arctic Home in the Vedas*. The other pairs are correct.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Hind Swaraj = Gandhi's first manifesto; Tilak = Gita Rahasya.

solvedExamples.q: How many players does each side have on court in a game of **volleyball**?
solvedExamples.solution: Volleyball is played **6-a-side**. Basketball has 5, kabaddi 7 and baseball/kho-kho 9.

solvedExamples.q: Who was the first recipient of the **Dadasaheb Phalke Award**, instituted in 1969?
solvedExamples.solution: Actress **Devika Rani** ('First Lady of Indian Cinema') received the first Phalke Award for 1969. Prithviraj Kapoor received it posthumously (1971), Raj Kapoor in 1987 and Satyajit Ray in 1984.
solvedExamples.shortcut: First Phalke = the First Lady of Indian cinema.

solvedExamples.q:
Match the organisations with their headquarters and choose the correct option.

A. UNESCO  B. UNEP  C. IAEA

1. Vienna  2. Paris  3. Nairobi
solvedExamples.solution: **UNESCO – Paris**, **UNEP – Nairobi**, **IAEA – Vienna** (also home to OPEC).
solvedExamples.shortcut: Fix UNESCO = Paris first — only option (a) and (c) have A-2; then UNEP = Nairobi settles it.

practice.q: The novel ***Godan*** was written by —
practice.solution: ***Godan*** (1936), Premchand's last completed novel, tells the story of the poor farmer Hori. Premchand also wrote *Gaban* and *Nirmala*.

practice.q: ***The God of Small Things***, winner of the 1997 Booker Prize, was written by —
practice.solution: **Arundhati Roy** won the Booker in **1997** for this Kerala-set debut novel. Kiran Desai won in 2006 for *The Inheritance of Loss*.

practice.q: ***Playing It My Way*** is the autobiography of —
practice.solution: ***Playing It My Way*** (2014) is **Sachin Tendulkar**'s autobiography, written with Boria Majumdar.
practice.shortcut: Sachin — 'my way' of playing for 24 years.

practice.q: ***Poverty and Un-British Rule in India***, which set out the 'drain of wealth' theory, was written by —
practice.solution: **Dadabhai Naoroji**, the 'Grand Old Man of India', published this book in 1901. R.C. Dutt wrote *The Economic History of India*.

practice.q: The **Santosh Trophy** is associated with —
practice.solution: The **Santosh Trophy** is India's national football championship for state teams, first held in 1941. The Ranji Trophy is its cricket counterpart.

practice.q: The **Uber Cup** is a world team championship for —
practice.solution: The **Uber Cup** is the women's world team badminton championship. The **Thomas Cup** is its men's version.

practice.q: The terms '**bully**' and '**penalty corner**' are associated with —
practice.solution: Both terms belong to **field hockey** — a bully restarts play between two players, and a penalty corner is awarded for defensive fouls inside the circle.
practice.shortcut: Penalty **corner** + bully = hockey (football has corner kicks, not penalty corners).

practice.q: Which Grand Slam tennis tournament is played on **clay courts**?
practice.solution: The **French Open** at Roland Garros, Paris is the only Grand Slam on **clay**. Wimbledon is on grass; the Australian and US Opens are on hard courts.

practice.q: Which shooter won India's **first individual Olympic gold medal**?
practice.solution: **Abhinav Bindra** won the **10 m air rifle** gold at **Beijing 2008**. Rathore won silver in 2004 (double trap); Narang and Vijay Kumar won medals in 2012.

practice.q: Which of the following received the **Bharat Ratna in 1954**, the first year of the award?
practice.solution: The 1954 recipients were **C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan and C.V. Raman**. Nehru got it in 1955; Ambedkar and Patel received it posthumously in 1990 and 1991.

practice.q: The **Dronacharya Award** is given for excellence in —
practice.solution: Instituted in **1985**, the Dronacharya Award honours **sports coaches**. The Arjuna Award is for sportspersons.
practice.shortcut: Drona was the guru (coach) of Arjuna — coach vs player.

practice.q: The first **Jnanpith Award** (1965) went to G. Sankara Kurup, who wrote in —
practice.solution: **G. Sankara Kurup** received the first Jnanpith for his **Malayalam** poetry collection *Odakkuzhal* ('The Bamboo Flute').

practice.q: **National Science Day** is celebrated in India on —
practice.solution: **28 February** marks C.V. Raman's discovery of the **Raman effect** in 1928. 7 November is Raman's birthday; 11 May is National Technology Day (Pokhran-II, 1998); 15 September is Engineers' Day.
practice.shortcut: Science Day = discovery date, not birthday.

practice.q: **National Sports Day** (29 August) is observed on the birth anniversary of —
practice.solution: Hockey wizard **Major Dhyan Chand** was born on 29 August 1905. The Khel Ratna is also named after him (since 2021).

practice.q: Who was the **first woman Governor** of an Indian state?
practice.solution: **Sarojini Naidu** became Governor of the United Provinces (now UP) in 1947. Sucheta Kriplani was the first woman Chief Minister (UP, 1963). Her daughter Padmaja Naidu later governed West Bengal.

practice.q: The motto '**Satyameva Jayate**' on India's national emblem is taken from the —
practice.solution: The words come from the **Mundaka Upanishad** ('Truth alone triumphs'). The emblem itself is adapted from Ashoka's Lion Capital at Sarnath.

practice.q: The currency of **Bhutan** is the —
practice.solution: Bhutan's currency is the **Ngultrum**, pegged at par with the Indian rupee. Taka = Bangladesh, Kyat = Myanmar, Rupiah = Indonesia.

practice.q: The headquarters of the **International Labour Organization (ILO)** is in —
practice.solution: The ILO, founded in **1919**, is based in **Geneva**, along with WHO and WTO.

practice.q: The **Knesset** is the parliament of —
practice.solution: The **Knesset** is Israel's unicameral legislature in Jerusalem. Iran – Majlis, Japan – Diet, Norway – Storting.

practice.q: The **Arthashastra**, the ancient treatise on statecraft, is attributed to:
practice.solution: **Kautilya (Chanakya)**, minister of Chandragupta Maurya, wrote the Arthashastra on polity, economy and spy-craft.

practice.q: **Indica**, an account of Mauryan India by a Greek envoy, was written by:
practice.solution: **Megasthenes**, ambassador of Seleucus Nicator at Chandragupta Maurya's court, wrote **Indica**; the original is lost but quoted by later writers.

practice.q: The **Harshacharita**, a biography of Emperor Harshavardhana, was composed by:
practice.solution: **Banabhatta**, Harsha's court poet, wrote the **Harshacharita** (and the prose romance Kadambari).

practice.q: Which Mughal emperor wrote his own memoir, the **Baburnama**?
practice.solution: **Babur** wrote the **Baburnama** himself in **Turkish**; the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is Jahangir's memoir; Akbar's story was written for him by Abul Fazl.

practice.q: The **Discovery of India** was written by:
practice.solution: **Nehru** wrote it during his Ahmednagar prison years (1942-46); his other book is **Glimpses of World History**.

practice.q: Who wrote **Hind Swaraj**, the classic statement of his political philosophy?
practice.solution: **Gandhi** wrote **Hind Swaraj** in 1909 aboard a ship from London to South Africa; his autobiography is *My Experiments with Truth*.

practice.q: **Gitanjali**, for which its author received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1913, is a collection of —
practice.solution: **Gitanjali** ('Song Offerings') is Tagore's collection of poems; he was the **first Asian** to win a Nobel Prize.

practice.q: **Wings of Fire** is the autobiography of:
practice.solution: **Wings of Fire** traces Kalam's journey from Rameswaram to ISRO, DRDO and the Rashtrapati Bhavan.

practice.q: **My Experiments with Truth** is the autobiography of:
practice.solution: Gandhi's autobiography, first published in Gujarati, is ***The Story of My Experiments with Truth***; Mandela's is *Long Walk to Freedom*.

practice.q: The autobiography **A Shot at History** is associated with which sportsperson?
practice.solution: **A Shot at History: My Obsessive Journey to Olympic Gold** - shooter **Abhinav Bindra**, co-written with Rohit Brijnath.

practice.q: Who wrote **Midnight's Children**, winner of the 1981 Booker Prize and later the 'Booker of Bookers'?
practice.solution: **Salman Rushdie's** Midnight's Children (1981) was judged the best Booker winner in 25 and 40 years of the prize.

practice.q: **The Inheritance of Loss**, which won the 2006 Booker Prize, was written by:
practice.solution: **Kiran Desai** won the 2006 Booker for The Inheritance of Loss; her mother **Anita Desai** was shortlisted several times but never won.

practice.q: **War and Peace** was written by the Russian novelist:
practice.solution: **Leo Tolstoy** wrote War and Peace; Dostoevsky wrote Crime and Punishment.

practice.q: Who wrote **Don Quixote**, often called the first modern novel?
practice.solution: **Cervantes** (Spain) wrote Don Quixote; Homer is the ancient Greek author of the Iliad and the Odyssey.

practice.q: **The Republic**, the foundational text of Western political philosophy, was written by:
practice.solution: **Plato's** The Republic discusses justice and the ideal state; Aristotle wrote Politics.

practice.q: The books **Animal Farm** and **Nineteen Eighty-Four** were written by:
practice.solution: **George Orwell** (Eric Blair) wrote both satires of totalitarianism; Huxley wrote Brave New World.

practice.q: The **Ranji Trophy** is associated with which sport?
practice.solution: The **Ranji Trophy** (since 1934) is India's premier first-class cricket championship, named after Ranjitsinhji.

practice.q: The **Sudirman Cup** is a world mixed-team championship of which sport?
practice.solution: **Sudirman Cup** = badminton mixed teams; **Thomas Cup** = men, **Uber Cup** = women.

practice.q: The **Ryder Cup** is a team competition in which sport, contested between the USA and Europe?
practice.solution: The **Ryder Cup** is golf's USA v Europe biennial match; the Davis Cup is tennis's equivalent for nations.

practice.q: The **Swaythling Cup** is awarded in which sport?
practice.solution: The **Swaythling Cup** goes to the men's team champion of world table tennis; the Corbillon Cup is the women's equivalent.

practice.q: The term '**bull's eye**' is associated with which sport?
practice.solution: A **bull's eye** is the centre of the target in archery and shooting events.

practice.q: The terms '**gambit**' and '**castling**' belong to which sport?
practice.solution: A **gambit** is an opening sacrifice, **castling** a king-rook move - both chess terms.

practice.q: '**Birdie**' and '**eagle**', terms for strokes under par, belong to which sport?
practice.solution: **Golf**: one under par = birdie, two under = eagle, one over = bogey.

practice.q: A **water polo** team has how many players in the pool?
practice.solution: **Water polo - seven** a side (six field players plus a goalkeeper). Kabaddi also fields seven.

practice.q: A **rugby union** team fields how many players?
practice.solution: **Rugby union - fifteen** a side; rugby league plays thirteen.

practice.q: Which team sport has exactly **four** players per side?
practice.solution: **Polo - four** mounted players a side. Basketball is five, kabaddi seven, baseball nine.

practice.q: Which Grand Slam tennis tournament is the **oldest**, first played in 1877?
practice.solution: **Wimbledon** (All England Club, London, grass) began in 1877 - the oldest tennis tournament in the world.

practice.q: The first **FIFA World Cup** football tournament (1930) was hosted and won by:
practice.solution: **Uruguay** hosted and won in 1930, beating Argentina in the final; the tournament is held every four years.

practice.q: The first **Cricket World Cup** (1975) was hosted by England. Which team won it?
practice.solution: The **West Indies**, captained by Clive Lloyd, beat Australia in the 1975 final at Lord's.

practice.q: The first modern **Olympic Games** (1896) were held in:
practice.solution: **Athens, 1896** - revived by Pierre de Coubertin; the IOC had been founded in Paris in 1894.

practice.q: The Olympic motto 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' means:
practice.solution: **Citius, Altius, Fortius** = Faster, Higher, Stronger (Latin); 'Communiter' (Together) was added in 2021.

practice.q: The **marathon** race in athletics is run over which distance?
practice.solution: **42.195 km**, fixed from the 1908 London route; the legend traces it to the Greek runner Pheidippides.

practice.q: Who won India's **first individual Olympic medal**, a wrestling bronze at Helsinki 1952?
practice.solution: **K.D. Jadhav** (wrestling, 1952 Helsinki) - India's first individual Olympic medal. Norman Pritchard had won two athletics silvers for India back in 1900.

practice.q: **Neeraj Chopra's** Tokyo 2020 gold medal came in which athletics event?
practice.solution: **Javelin throw** - his winning throw measured **87.58 m**; it was India's second-ever individual Olympic gold.

practice.q: India's first chess **Grandmaster** (1988) is:
practice.solution: **Viswanathan Anand** became India's first GM in 1988; he later won the world championship in multiple formats.

practice.q: Which of the following is the **highest civilian award** of India?
practice.solution: **Bharat Ratna** ('Jewel of India') is the highest civilian award; the Param Vir Chakra is the highest *wartime gallantry* award.

practice.q: The **first woman** to receive the Bharat Ratna was:
practice.solution: **Indira Gandhi** (1971). Mother Teresa received it in 1980; M.S. Subbulakshmi in 1998.

practice.q: The Padma awards, in descending order of precedence, are:
practice.solution: **Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri**, all instituted in 1954, below the Bharat Ratna.

practice.q: Who was the **first Indian** to win the Nobel Prize in Physics?
practice.solution: **C.V. Raman** (1930) for the Raman effect; Tagore's 1913 prize was in Literature.

practice.q: **Kailash Satyarthi** shared the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize with —
practice.solution: Satyarthi (child rights) shared it with **Malala Yousafzai** (Pakistan) - education for all children.

practice.q: Who is the only person to have won **two Nobel Prizes in different sciences**?
practice.solution: **Marie Curie** - Physics 1903 and Chemistry 1911; the first woman laureate. (Pauling and Bardeen also won two Nobels, but one of theirs was Peace or in the same field.)

practice.q: India's **highest wartime gallantry award** is the:
practice.solution: **Param Vir Chakra** - literally 'wheel of the supreme hero'; the Ashoka Chakra is its peacetime counterpart.

practice.q: The **first Param Vir Chakra** was awarded posthumously to which officer of the 1947-48 Kashmir operations?
practice.solution: **Major Somnath Sharma** (Kumaon Regiment) fell at Badgam, November 1947 - the first PVC.

practice.q: India's **highest award in cinema** is the:
options: National Film Award for Best Feature Film
practice.solution: The **Dadasaheb Phalke Award** (from 1969) honours lifetime contribution to Indian cinema; the first went to Devika Rani.

practice.q: The **Abel Prize**, since 2003 called the 'Nobel of mathematics', is awarded by which country?
practice.solution: **Norway** (by its Academy of Science and Letters) gives the Abel Prize; the Fields Medal is the other great mathematics award.

practice.q: The **Ramon Magsaysay Award**, often called the 'Asian Nobel', is given by which country's foundation?
practice.solution: The **Philippines** (Ramon Magsaysay Award Foundation, Manila), from 1958, in memory of President Magsaysay.

practice.q: The first **Gandhi Peace Prize** (1995), instituted by the Government of India, went to:
practice.solution: **Julius Nyerere**, former President of Tanzania, won the first Gandhi Peace Prize (1995).

practice.q: Who was the **first recipient** of India's highest sporting honour (Khel Ratna), in 1991-92?
practice.solution: Chess world champion **Viswanathan Anand** received the first Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (1991-92); renamed after Major Dhyan Chand in 2021.

practice.q: The **Dhyan Chand Award** is given for —
practice.solution: **Dhyan Chand Award** = lifetime contribution to sport; Dronacharya = coaches; Arjuna = players; MAKA = universities.

practice.q: **Teachers' Day** in India (5 September) is the birth anniversary of:
practice.solution: Dr **S. Radhakrishnan**, philosopher and second President, was born on 5 September 1888; since 1962 the day honours teachers.

practice.q: **National Youth Day** (12 January) marks the birth anniversary of:
practice.solution: **Swami Vivekananda** (born 12 January 1863); the date also opens the National Youth Festival.

practice.q: **Engineers' Day** (15 September) commemorates the birth of which engineer?
practice.solution: Sir **M. Visvesvaraya** (1861), knighted engineer of the Krishna Raja Sagara dam and automatic sluices.

practice.q: **National Doctors' Day** (1 July) honours which physician-statesman?
practice.solution: Dr **Bidhan Chandra Roy**, physician and West Bengal Chief Minister, born and died on 1 July; a Bharat Ratna recipient (1961).

practice.q: **National Technology Day** (11 May) recalls which event of 1998?
practice.solution: Operation Shakti's **Pokhran-II tests** of **11 May 1998**; the day celebrates Indian technology.

practice.q: **Hindi Diwas** is observed on 14 September because on that day in 1949 —
options: Hindi was adopted as the official language of the Union
The Sahitya Akademi was set up
practice.solution: The Constituent Assembly adopted **Hindi in Devanagari script** as the official language of the Union on **14 September 1949** (Article 343).

practice.q: **National Voters' Day** (25 January) marks the founding day of the:
practice.solution: The **Election Commission was constituted on 25 January 1950**; Voters' Day has been observed on the date since 2011.

practice.q: **International Yoga Day** is observed on:
practice.solution: **21 June**, the longest day in the north - first observed in **2015** after India's proposal at the UN (2014).

practice.q: **World Food Day** (16 October) is linked to the founding of which organisation?
practice.solution: The **Food and Agriculture Organization** was founded on **16 October 1945** in Rome, its permanent headquarters city.

practice.q: **Human Rights Day** (10 December) commemorates the adoption in 1948 of the:
practice.solution: The **UDHR** was adopted by the UN General Assembly in Paris on **10 December 1948**.

practice.q: **World Water Day** falls on which date?
practice.solution: **22 March** (since 1993). 22 April is Earth Day; 5 June is Environment Day.

practice.q: **Indian Air Force Day** is observed on —
practice.solution: The **IAF was founded on 8 October 1932**; Army Day - 15 January; Navy Day - 4 December.

practice.q: **Army Day** (15 January) recalls the day in 1949 when:
options: K.M. Cariappa became the first Indian Commander-in-Chief
practice.solution: General **K.M. Cariappa** (later Field Marshal) took over from General Sir Francis Butcher on **15 January 1949**.

practice.q: **Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas)** is observed on 26 November, the day the Constitution was —
practice.solution: Adopted **26 November 1949**; it **came into force on 26 January 1950**, which is Republic Day.

practice.q: Republic Day is fixed on 26 January to honour the **Purna Swaraj** declaration of independence, first publicly celebrated on 26 January of which year?
practice.solution: The Congress declared Purna Swaraj at its **Lahore session (December 1929)**; the first Independence Day was observed on **26 January 1930**, hence the date for Republic Day.

practice.q: The **national aquatic animal** of India is the:
practice.solution: The **Gangetic river dolphin** was declared national aquatic animal in 2009; the Ganga is the national river (2008).

practice.q: Which of the following is India's **national tree**?
practice.solution: The **banyan** (Ficus benghalensis) - longevity and rootedness; the mango is the national fruit.

practice.q: The **Saka calendar**, used in official gazettes alongside the Gregorian calendar, was adopted in —
practice.solution: Adopted from **22 March 1957** (= 1 Chaitra 1879 Saka) on the Calendar Reform Committee's recommendation.

practice.q: The Indian national flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
practice.solution: **22 July 1947** - about a fortnight before Independence; the ratio is 3:2.

practice.q: Who designed the present form of the **Indian national flag**?
practice.solution: **Pingali Venkayya** of Andhra, whose design (with Gandhi's suggested additions) became the tricolour.

practice.q: In the national flag, the **navy-blue Ashoka Chakra** stands for —
options: Progress and motion (the wheel of law)
practice.solution: The chakra represents the **wheel of law (dharma)** and constant movement forward; the 24 spokes evoke the hours of the day.

practice.q: *Vande Mataram*, India's national song, is taken from Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's novel —
practice.solution: ***Anandamath*** (1882); the song was first sung at the 1896 Calcutta session of the Congress.

practice.q: The State Emblem of India is adapted from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at —
practice.solution: The **Sarnath** capital (four lions on an abacus), adopted on 26 January 1950 with the motto Satyameva Jayate.

practice.q: The words **'Satyameva Jayate'** on the state emblem are taken from:
practice.solution: The **Mundaka Upanishad** - 'truth alone triumphs'.

practice.q: Who was the **first woman Speaker** of the Lok Sabha?
practice.solution: **Meira Kumar** (2009-14); Sumitra Mahajan followed her in the chair.

practice.q: The **first Indian woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest** (1984) was:
practice.solution: **Bachendri Pal** (Tata group mountaineer) climbed Everest in May 1984; Santosh Yadav summited twice later.

practice.q: Who was the **first woman President of the Indian National Congress**?
practice.solution: **Annie Besant** presided over the Calcutta session in 1917; **Sarojini Naidu** was the first Indian woman, in 1925 (Kanpur session).

practice.q: India's **first Prime Minister** was:
practice.solution: **Nehru** (1947-64), also the longest-serving Prime Minister; Rajendra Prasad was the first President.

practice.q: The **first Indian satellite**, launched in 1975, was named:
practice.solution: **Aryabhata**, launched (from a Soviet rocket) in 1975 and named after the ancient astronomer.

practice.q: **23 August**, the day Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole (2023), is observed as —
practice.solution: **National Space Day** - the Vikram lander touched down on 23 August 2023, making India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon.

practice.q: India's **first passenger train** ran in 1853 between:
practice.solution: **16 April 1853** - 34 km from Bombay (Bori Bunder) to Thane; the first railway company had been formed in 1849.

practice.q: Who was the **first Indian to travel into space** (1984)?
practice.solution: Sqn Ldr **Rakesh Sharma** flew on the Soviet Soyuz T-11 in 1984; his reply from orbit - 'saare jahaan se achha'. Ravish Malhotra was his backup.

practice.q: The headquarters of **UNESCO** are in:
practice.solution: **UNESCO - Paris**; UNICEF and UNDP sit at New York; WHO and WTO at Geneva.

practice.q: The **Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)** is headquartered in:
practice.solution: **Rome** (Italy) - shared with the World Food Programme; UNEP alone is in Nairobi.

practice.q: Which specialised agency of the UN is headquartered in **Nairobi**?
practice.solution: The **UN Environment Programme** - making Nairobi the only UN headquarters city in the Global South.

practice.q: The headquarters of **SAARC** are at:
practice.solution: **SAARC - Kathmandu** (founded 1985); BIMSTEC's secretariat is in Dhaka.

practice.q: The **Asian Development Bank (ADB)** is headquartered at:
practice.solution: **ADB - Manila** (1966). AIIB sits in Beijing and the NDB (BRICS bank) in Shanghai.

practice.q: The **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** is headquartered at:
practice.solution: **Lausanne**, Switzerland - the 'Olympic Capital'; FIFA's HQ is in Zurich.

practice.q: **INTERPOL**, the international police organisation (founded 1923), has its headquarters at:
practice.solution: **INTERPOL - Lyon, France** (it began in Vienna in 1923). The Hague hosts the ICJ and OPCW.

practice.q: The currency of **Bangladesh** is the:
practice.solution: **Taka**. The rupiah belongs to Indonesia; the rupee to India, Pakistan, Nepal and Sri Lanka.

practice.q: The currency of **Myanmar** is the:
practice.solution: **Kyat**. Thailand - baht; Laos - kip; Malaysia - ringgit.

practice.q: The currency of **South Africa** is the:
practice.solution: **Rand**. Nigeria - naira; Kenya - shilling; Botswana - pula.

practice.q: Which country's currency is the **real**?
practice.solution: **Brazil** uses the real; Mexico and Argentina use pesos; Chile the Chilean peso.

practice.q: The **Diet** is the national legislature of:
practice.solution: Japan's parliament is the **Diet** (House of Representatives + House of Councillors); China's is the National People's Congress.

practice.q: The parliament of **Iran** is known as the:
practice.solution: Iran's parliament is the **Majlis**; Pakistan's federal legislature is the Majlis-e-Shoora.

practice.q: The **Folketing** is the parliament of which country?
practice.solution: **Denmark - Folketing**; Norway - Storting; Sweden - Riksdag.

practice.q: The lower house of Russia's Federal Assembly is called the:
practice.solution: The **State Duma** is the lower house; the Federation Council is the upper house. (Gosplan was the Soviet planning body.)

practice.q: The **World Health Organization** was established in:
practice.solution: **WHO - 7 April 1948** (hence World Health Day); it sits in Geneva.

practice.q: **ASEAN**, the association of South-East Asian nations, was founded in 1967 at:
practice.solution: Founded at **Bangkok** by the five original members (Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand); its headquarters are in **Jakarta**.

practice.q: Which pair of organisations was created together at the **Bretton Woods Conference** (1944)?
practice.solution: The **Bretton Woods twins** - the IMF and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (now the World Bank), both seated at Washington DC.
